key_insight: The paper shows that controlling and strategically injecting bias can make multi-agent LLM aggregation more reliable when agents disagree.
engineering_relevance: It offers a test-time, training-free aggregation method that improves answer accuracy and token efficiency without needing validation data or model-strength priors.
method: Normalize each distinct answer into a style-matched reasoning trace before aggregation.
Use bias control to reduce non-semantic effects like majority pressure and response-style preference.
Use bias injection by making each agent’s initial choice the minority to expose decision instability as a reliability signal.
evidence_signal: Across three mathematical reasoning benchmarks and four heterogeneous LLM pairings, the framework outperforms non-oracle aggregation methods and also improves multi-agent debate and Mixture-of-Agents final-answer accuracy.
watch_item: The method depends on manipulating presentation order and minority status, so its gains may vary with prompt sensitivity and heterogeneous agent behavior.
paper_title: Bias Control and Injection for Multi-Agent Aggregation
